speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing frequent nosebleeds, bleeding from your gums or other mucous membranes, and small red spots on your skin. To help me understand what might be causing these symptoms, could you tell me your age and if you have noticed any unusual bruising or bleeding after minor injuries?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you. Has the child had any recent fevers, infections, or fatigue, and have you noticed any swelling in the abdomen or joints?

REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal platelet count rules out thrombocytopenia, so we must look at coagulation factors. Is there a family history of bleeding disorders, and do the nosebleeds tend to stop with direct pressure?

REQUEST TEST: PT, PTT, Factor_VIII_Activity

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: PT: 12 seconds (normal), aPTT: 30 seconds (normal), Factor_VIII_Activity: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal coagulation studies and platelet count strongly suggest a platelet function disorder rather than a clotting factor deficiency. Do you have a family history of bleeding issues, and does the child have a history of frequent or severe bleeding after minor cuts or dental procedures?

REQUEST TEST: Bleeding_Time, Platelet_Function_Assay

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Bleeding_Time: Prolonged, Platelet_Function_Assay: Abnormal aggregation response to ADP, epinephrine, and collagen; normal aggregation response to ristocetin

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal ristocetin aggregation effectively rules out von Willebrand disease, while the abnormal response to other agonists points toward a specific platelet signaling defect. This pattern is characteristic of Glanzmann thrombasthenia, a defect in the GPIIb/IIIa complex.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Glanzmann thrombasthenia
